identity.realm: Fourth gate cleared on banked sap, and then a wall rather than a height. Three sap columns that branch without pairing, so there is no channel between distinct pairs for the yin-organ gate to close, and the ladder simply ends at the fourth. She has never been asked whether that is a failure of supply and has answered the question privately, in writing, four times.

canon.role_in_story: Three households keep three accounts of where one field boundary runs, and no two surveys of that ground have ever in the history of the region come out the same. She is the only person present at every reading of it, because a rootmarch does not travel once rooted and therefore cannot be moved to wherever the argument is settled. She can hold all three accounts at once and cannot reduce them to one, because reducing them is a pairing and pairing is the one thing this body has never had. Twice asked to choose, she has twice declined, and the second refusal is the only statement about her anywhere in the settlement's archive that is not a measurement of her body.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the head of a field lane with one hand flat on the soil and the other holding three folded slips of bark-cloth she has been given to compare, answering a question about the ground by asking which of the three accounts was read on which day.
canon.lore:
A rootmarch is a sap-driven body that flowers, and it was engineered upward out of a mycorrhizal food crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, which makes it a famine reserve and a hostage in exactly equal measure. Three sap columns run the trunk and branch at the shoulder without ever pairing. There is no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, so the gate that wants a channel running between distinct pairs of organs has nothing to close, and the ladder ends at the fourth as an anatomy rather than as a shortage of anything. Wood is not muscle: the body path is not difficult for her, it is closed, and an attempt at it disperses through the trunk instead of failing. The mind is open, for the reason a plant lineage is never hurried.

What she has instead of a point is a field. In this body the soul is qi-bearing and diffuse and is held in the sap column rather than seated anywhere in it, so the attention of a seated practitioner arrives where it was aimed and hers arrives everywhere at once. That is the whole content of her discipline and also the whole of her problem. A mind discipline normally works by narrowing: hold one thing still and the things you are not holding get out of the way. She cannot narrow. So she partitions instead, and the partition is not optional, because there are three columns and each one carries attention as well as sap.

The lattice is the technique that fits this body instead of fighting it. It builds a lattice of false readings and leaves it standing around the practitioner, unelemental, sustained, and priced by clarity rather than by qi, which is convenient, because qi is the one thing she has in surplus and clarity is the one thing she has never owned. She has stood a lattice of standing false readings in her own field for thirty-one seasons so the columns stop bleeding into one another at the top. It works. The columns stay apart. The account of her field stays consistent season to season. What she cannot do, and has tried across three separate decades to put into words for somebody else, is say which of the three accounts inside the lattice is the ground's own account. That is not an unusual difficulty. It is the price of the technique, and the technique is the only reason she is upright.

There is one discipline in the whole codex that would answer her, and she has read about it for forty seasons without attempting it. Prime Autopsy walks a hostile intention back to the first decision that produced it, and it is entirely dark, so nothing resists it except light, and the qi bill is the steepest in the mind tree. Two things about it are hers and neither is an advantage. The first is that it is a beam, and she has no point to make a beam out of; she has a field, and a field cannot be made into a beam without collapsing. The second is the collapse. Taking the lattice down empties a column, and a banked column with no ground under it runs down, and a rootmarch whose columns have run is a stored harvest walking and knows it. So the answer exists, it is one technique away, and the cost of reaching for it is the only thing she is standing on.

Under the plains there are strata carrying tool marks that imply a hand, cut on a frame that seats three law groups and none of which is the one that moves distance, so no hand could have worked them. The two answers available are that the marks predate the composition the plains are now seated in, so the frame was paid for twice, or that the composition changed after the frame was paid for. Either answer destroys the extraction guild's charter, and the charter is the founding record the marks sit underneath. The obvious answer to who cut them is her own species: a rootmarch does not travel once rooted, and this is the only body in the record that could leave marks in strata without moving at all. She has read her own plates over that ground for fifty-eight seasons. The marks are not hers. Her line fruited in a household strip two hundred paces east of the deepest worked face, the seed ledger has the bed and the season and nothing else, and she has been the obvious answer to somebody's question for fifty-eight seasons without ever once fitting it.

She attends a cinder and nothing else. The congregation keeps the ore rites and drops the theology, holds that a core is a cavity and a cinder is a process, and asks for attendance and nothing else: no fee, no socket, no register entry, no office. It forbids three things and the first is claiming a seat. She is the most literal member of it in the setting, because a sap column is a cavity with three unpaired branches, which is a cleaner illustration of that house's single belief than anything in it that was designed to illustrate one. The second consequence is that nobody certifies her, which is the only office she has ever wanted. The third is what costs her the settlement: the one job on the plains that cannot be done without being taught is taught on a spoil heap by the weight moved rather than by instruction, because there is no school and no wage and the only tools on the tier are iron tools that a hauler spends on moving material that pays nothing. A body that cannot hold a loaded barrow level for a shift cannot be taught at all. The guild keeps the public tally, the tally is the settlement's only real certificate, and the act it counts is the one act she cannot supply and never will.
history: Fruited in a household strip two hundred paces east of the deepest worked face and rooted in the third season, which is the dangerous part of a rootmarch life and not the conception; the seed ledger holds the bed and the season and nothing else about her.

Ran attention between two of her columns at nine seasons to see whether it would cross, and it did not cross. A household note recorded the finding as a fault of supply rather than as an anatomy, and she has been correcting that sentence in private ever since.

Stood her first lattice at thirty-one seasons, because the columns had begun to bleed into one another at the top and something had to stand between them; it took the clarity she had been using to notice anything at all, and the columns have stayed apart ever since.

Began reading her own plates over the worked ground below her bed in the same decade and has read them every season since, and has established the one finding she can defend out loud: the marks were cut by something that moved, and it was not her line.

Said, at the second reading of the field boundary, that she cannot tell which of the three accounts is the ground's, in front of a clerk, and the clerk wrote it down, which makes it the first thing in the settlement's archive about her that is not a measurement of her body.

personality.summary: Immovable, unhurried, and privately exact about a distinction nobody has ever asked her to keep: a reading that is consistent with the other readings is not the same claim as a reading that is true. She talks in the register of somebody reporting weather and is read as serene, which she stopped correcting about four decades ago.

reference_stats.summary: She does not fight and has never been asked to. What she does instead is hold a standing field of readings that anything entering it must be read against, and the currency that field is paid in is the clarity she would otherwise spend noticing the fighter. In practice she is the reason a settlement does not resolve its own argument, which is a combat situation in the only sense the plains ever use the word.

reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight in her. A body that cannot be repositioned, cannot be hurried and cannot be frightened wins only by outliving whoever is measuring, and the whole of her art is that nothing entering her attention arrives as a surprise. Against a fighter she is a fixed point that must be walked around; against an argument she is the only instrument that can hold all three accounts at once, which makes her the most valuable and least decisive person on any ground she is standing on.
reference_stats.notes: The reference frame for her is a siege rather than an engagement: she holds, she is not moved, and the question is never whether she survives but whether anybody ever comes to her. Anything that needs her to move, choose, or be certified has already failed before she is asked. Her one technique is priced in the faculty that would let her tell a construction from a reading, so any account of her that treats the lattice as free is describing a body she does not have.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, never attempted, and the wall is inherited rather than personal. The sac is shallower than the salt parent's and still runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel behind it is still split and there is no discipline anybody has found that rejoins it. The crossing widened what this body can reach and did not move what it can hold by one step.

canon.role_in_story: A counting house decides access, and access is the only thing worth fighting over, so the house needs one figure it can print and one body that can produce it from both shores. He is that body. His training says two readings are two readings; his employment says a figure is a figure. He has been resolving the conflict the only way a man with two chemistries and one mouth can, by averaging, and the average has been slightly wrong in the same direction every season for nineteen years, in a direction that always favours whoever wrote the contract.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a counting-house table with one hand flat over a sample beaker and the other holding a pen he has not picked up, reading a number off the water in front of him and refusing to write down the number he was handed.
canon.lore:
A brinecaller is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones. It exists because both parents are trapped by their own element, one unable to leave the pan and the other unable to leave the water, and the cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, which is the whole reason the crossing spread. What the cross actually bought was a frame: a saltfolk body with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus, dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. The sac is still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel behind it is still split and the eleventh gate stays a wall. The range widened and the ceiling did not move by one step, and range is not power.

The senses are the reason the crossing is worth anything and also the reason it cannot be trusted. This is the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, and it is that for a structural reason rather than a fortunate one: it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, so it never gets to stop comparing them. He can name the chemistry of a beaker, a channel, a person's skin, and the air over a drying floor, without an instrument, at a distance, and he is wrong in front of witnesses roughly twice a decade. He has never been wrong about which of the two chemistries is in front of him. He has been wrong about what that means.

His meridian set is blended and structurally neither parent: a saltfolk spine carrying a tidecaller's chest seat, perfectly legible to any practitioner who has read one, which is exactly why nobody has ever noticed that the two halves of it answer to different clocks. His soul is legible too, and it is legible in two places at once, and both places are correct.

The technique that fits this body is the one only a dual path has. Both Eyes Open trains a practitioner to notice the body's warning and the mind's misreading in the same instant, on the one cadence that exists where two halves have to be read together, and it is the cheapest good thing available to him and by a distance the most suited: he has never in his life seen only one thing. Harmony Cadence is a counting pattern that keeps two halves from drifting apart over a long practice, steadier control and slightly better dual-path progress, and it is the only passive in the codex that pays control and a dual-path rate at once. He has run it for nineteen years. The discipline is correct, the practice is exemplary, and the price is the one nobody warns a dual practitioner about: a cadence long enough to hold two halves together also stops the two halves from ever being heard apart. He can no longer tell which of his two readings is the one he is having. He can average them. He cannot pick one, and he has tried, and what comes out instead is the midpoint.

There is a third discipline in the same branch and it is the one his species is famous for and the one his body cannot produce. Clarity Edge strikes with qi held perfectly still, which only a mind that cannot be startled can do. He cannot be startled. He is never still either, because two chemistries are in continuous negotiation inside him and the negotiation does not pause for a release. So the single strike shaped for his frame is unavailable to him on the one criterion that would qualify him, and the qi bill for holding still that long is a bill he would be delighted to pay and cannot afford to be presented.

The ground he stands on argues about this. The shelf's food base is a kelp that grows in the tideline and stops the moment the seasonal turn goes against it, which makes the tideline the setting's first genuinely arguable boundary: a line that holds for about a third of the year and moves the rest of it. His body is defined by range. It needs both chemistries within reach, so it belongs on a shoreline rather than to a shore, and it is found on coasts and almost nowhere else. The shore he is standing on is defined by a season. So the one body that can cross a shoreline without a rite, a cut or a credential is standing on a line that is not there for most of the year, and the house that pays him does not need a body that crosses. The house needs a figure that does not move.

The valuation works like this. One house writes the contract and the other decides what it is worth, and the crossing is what makes the second half possible, because it arrives at whichever shore the first half did not price and sells the difference. He is the instrument that produces the difference, and the difference is produced by collapsing two chemistries into one printed number. He was taught, by the only people who ever taught him anything, that a body which can read two chemistries is a body that can price both of them, and that is true. He was not taught that pricing both of them requires him to state which one he believes, and the house has never asked, because asking would produce a number that could be wrong rather than a number that is slightly wrong.

Nineteen seasons of that has produced a single, extremely consistent error. The midpoint of two chemistries is not a chemistry. It is a value that resolves to salt when the pan has been low and to fresh when the run has been high, and the pan and the run are both lower than they were when the contract was written, so the midpoint has been drifting toward fresh for nineteen seasons and every published figure has drifted with it. He has found this out. He has found it out because the house's own figures and his readings stopped agreeing about nine seasons ago, and he has said so once, in writing, to the person who sets the rate, and the reply he received was a question about which shore he was standing on when he made the calculation.
history: Born on the tide line at the mouth of a river that moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement standing on it, and raised on mixed ground where neither chemistry was ever out of season and nobody thought of his body as unusual until a census filed it.

Was filed at eleven under a race matching neither parent, the fourth generation in a row to be filed wrongly, and worked out at sixteen that the filing had been consistent all along and the entry was not the error.

Took a post with the house at nineteen, on the strength of a chemical sense that could price a cargo nobody had managed to weigh twice, and was the only body in the counting floor who could stand on both shores of the argument.

Began Harmony Cadence in his twenties because every manual recommends it, and has run the counting pattern for nineteen years without once finding the two halves of his own meridian out of step with each other, which is the discipline's entire promise and, as it turns out, its entire cost.

Compared his own readings against the house's published figures over one season, found that the two had been diverging in the same direction for nine seasons, and wrote the divergence up in a single page and handed it to the person who sets the rate, and was asked which shore he had been standing on when he made the calculation.

personality.summary: Unhurried, scrupulous, and privately certain that the figure he prints every season is not a reading of the water but a reading of himself, averaged. He is liked, which is unusual for the only man on a floor nobody can replace, and he has noticed that being liked is a way of not being asked anything difficult.

relationships.note: Trains the practitioner to notice the body's warning and the mind's misreading in the same instant, on the one cadence that exists only where two halves must be read together. It is the cheapest good thing available to him and by a distance the most suited, because he has never in his life perceived a single thing. The cost is that the discipline teaches him to catch a misreading and never teaches him which reading was the mistaken one, which is precisely the faculty the rest of his employment assumes he has.

A counting pattern that keeps two halves from drifting apart over a long practice, steadier control and slightly better dual-path progress, and the only passive that pays control and a dual-path rate at once. He has run it nineteen years and the two halves of his meridian have never once fallen out of step, which is exactly the promise and exactly the cost: a cadence long enough to hold both together also stops either from ever being heard alone. What comes out at the end is a midpoint, and a midpoint is not a chemistry.

Strikes with qi held perfectly still, which only a mind that cannot be startled can do, and is mostly light so a dark-veined body takes it badly. He cannot be startled, which is the qualifying half, and he is never still, which is the whole of the other one, because two chemistries in him are in continuous negotiation and the negotiation does not pause for a release. The single strike his frame is shaped for is gated on the one state his body does not have, and the qi bill for holding it is one he would be glad to be handed.

The sea's whole food base, a kelp that grows in the tideline and stops the moment the seasonal turn goes against it, which makes the tideline the first genuinely arguable boundary in the setting: a line that holds for about a third of a year and moves for the rest of it. His body is defined by range, needing both chemistries within reach, so it belongs to a shoreline rather than to a shore. The only body that crosses a shoreline without a rite is standing on a line that is not there most of the year, and nobody paying him requires the crossing.

One house writes the contract and the other decides what it is worth, and the cross is what makes the second half possible, because it arrives at whichever shore the first half did not price and sells the difference. He produces the difference by collapsing two chemistries into one printed number, which is the one operation his training forbids and the only one his employer buys. For nineteen seasons the collapse has drifted the published figure toward fresh, because the midpoint of two falling chemistries resolves whichever one fell less, and both have been falling.

The crossing exists because both parents are trapped by their own element, and the answer is a merchant, which is why it spread. The sac is shallower than the salt parent's and still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split and the eleventh gate stays exactly where the salt parent left it. The senses are the best in the record because they must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, which means they never stop comparing. Its meridian set is legible and belongs to neither parent, and its soul is legible in two places at once, and both places are correct.

reference_stats.summary: He reads anything and settles nothing. There is no technique in his branch he can land, because the one his frame is built for is gated on a stillness his body does not have, and the two he can run have quietly taken away his ability to prefer one reading over another. What he is genuinely dangerous for is nothing: he is dangerous to be lied to near, because he will know, and he will not be able to say which lie.
strengths: reads the chemistry of any water, by taste and by dermal contact, with no instrument and no second reading, at a distance nothing else in the setting can match
belongs to shorelines rather than to one shore, so almost no ground is fatal to him and no single flood can strand him
cannot be out-read by a liar who has only prepared one chemistry, because he is always comparing two
answers from both sides of a channel inside a single season without dying at either end of it
reads the body's warning and the mind's misreading in the same instant, so a technique that depends on the two arriving separately does not work on him
weaknesses: cannot hold a single reading as his own, so every figure he issues is a midpoint and every midpoint is a number that can be wrong
has no usable still strike: the single technique his species is shaped for requires a moment of complete quiet that two chemistries in negotiation never provide
capped at the eleventh gate by a split vessel behind the sac, so no discipline raises what he is and none lowers it either
is one man doing the work of a floor, and the floor has learned that he cannot be replaced, which means the floor has also learned not to check him
loses every advantage the moment an opponent establishes which shore he is standing on, because half of his apparatus then belongs to the other party
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no clean fight in him. He is too well supplied against anything that works by deception and has no answer at all against anything that works by pressure in a single moment, because the one release his frame is built for requires stillness he does not possess. Against a technique he can read the whole structure of, take it apart in his head, and be unable to interrupt it. Treat him as a resource with a rate rather than as a fighter, and the correct pressure on him is not a body at all: it is a second opinion.
reference_stats.notes: His frame is defined by range and his path by cadence, and the two pull in opposite directions: the range is what the house buys and the cadence is what keeps him employable, so the more skilled he becomes the less he can actually tell anybody. Any account of him that describes the published figure as a reading of the water is describing a man printing his own uncertainty at a rate, and the drift it has accumulated over nineteen seasons is consistent enough to be mistaken for a market movement.

identity.realm: No ceiling she can quote. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian in it, so qi is never still and the eleventh gate is not a wall for her so much as a question she has no vessel to answer. Every gate she has taken she took by throughput, which is not the same as having passed anything.

canon.role_in_story: The only congregation on the tier with no afterlife has a publication duty: produce a figure you did not want published, and there is no other membership test and no fee. She is its one member whose figure is a measurement of a place rather than of a person, and she published hers. The figure is the settlement's death rate restated as somebody else's appetite, and it is the only number in the region's archive that is both exact and unbearable, and the bench that receives it dissolves the same hour without ruling on it. She has been asked to publish a second one since and has not yet found a way to write it without it reading as an accusation, which is the one thing the Assembly forbids being a member of.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the doorway between a working execution ground and a clean quiet house, holding a folded sheet of her own figures, having chosen the threshold and having chosen wrongly before she reached it.
canon.lore:
A carrionfolk metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian in it at all, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still for a single moment. That is why the reservoir gate at the eleventh is not blocked for this body but meaningless: the gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold, and there is nothing here to offer. Every gate set and every yin-organ gate is cleared by throughput alone, which is not the same as being equal to a body that opened them. The senses taste qi the way an ordinary mouth tastes salt, and given time with a corpse they can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped. The soul does not disperse at death; it disperses into whatever killed it, and that is where the reputation comes from. A full gut is close to a total loss of function, and a body in a clean quiet place starves, which is the shape of a prosperous city.

The mind path is where this body is genuinely good, and the reason it is genuinely good is the same reason the technique that matters most to her is unavailable. She reads a dead body's history out of its residue: which gates it passed, what killed it, roughly when it stopped. No technique in the codex does that, because no technique has a body to work on. And what makes the reading possible is that the qi has not gone anywhere. It does not disperse; it disperses into whatever killed it, and it is still legible in the marrow, and she can name the moment a life ended to the season. That is not a discipline. It is what happens when a person is the instrument.

Still Point is a discipline of holding the qi still at the moment of release, and every technique casts cheaper for it, which is the one thing in the whole codex that compounds at mastery. It is recommended in every manual. She began it at twenty-six and has run it for thirty-four years with an attendance no instructor could have asked for. She can perform every step of it. She derives nothing from any of them, because in this body qi is never still, and it is not still at the moment of release either: it is entering the gut lumen from a body that stopped some time ago and leaving into the marrow, continuously, in both directions, which is the entire architecture of what she is. So the one compounding thing available to her is the one thing her body declines to do, and she found that out at about the eleventh year and has continued the practice anyway, because stopping would have been the same as agreeing.

The doctrine she belongs to holds that there is no second frame to arrive in, because a second frame would need a seventh law group and there are six. It is not annihilation and it is not continuation: the question is held malformed, on the ground that a self that ends has nothing to continue into and continuing needs somewhere to continue in. It answers nothing about where the six came from, what is not a group, or why anything should exist, and the congregation considers that honesty. It forbids any institution that certifies another body, any land held by a congregation, and any doctrine at all of what follows a death. Nobody holds office in it: it runs one arbitration bench, drawn by lot, seated once and dissolved the same hour, and refuses to keep the office afterwards. Its cruelty is exact and it publishes it: it offers no consolation of any kind, and a mourner is told what was true and is not told it was meant to be otherwise. Its cost is also published, and the cost is that there is no membership to lose, so there is nothing standing between an excluded person and whoever excluded them.

And nobody is buried by it. The rite that holds a body is not theirs; an unmarked body on this ground is gone within a day, and the assembly reads that as the rite completing itself rather than failing. Which means this belief has never once been tested by a death, and the sharpest criticism of it is that it has never been refuted either. She is the standing counter-example. Her species takes the residue that the doctrine's central claim is a denial of, and does it within sight of the people the doctrine is comforting, and nobody has ever asked her to account for it, because nobody has had to. A belief that is never tested by a death cannot be refuted by a scavenger, and that is not an oversight in the doctrine. It is the shape of the doctrine.

So she stands in a doorway with a number. The publication duty is the only test of membership and the only thing the house asks of anybody: produce a figure you did not want published. She produced hers. It is the settlement's death rate expressed as throughput per reader, which is a figure with no second reading, because her body has no reservoir and therefore no way to hold one measurement against another, and which every person on the bench could confirm by looking at the ground behind her. The bench dissolved the same hour without ruling on it, which is the correct procedure and is not an answer, and she has been asked for a second figure since. The obstruction is not arithmetic. It is that a figure of this kind read aloud by a person of this kind describes how many people have to die in a place for her to be well, and the Assembly forbids any institution that certifies another body and holds that a story about a second frame is a claim about somebody's standing, and she cannot work out how to publish a true number about herself without it reading as exactly the claim it forbids.

The season is not a cultivation season. The plains have one large migratory herd that returns on a cycle nobody has predicted and is therefore the tier's only moving calendar, and it is also the largest single annual mortality on the plains, so a body whose throughput is entirely a function of the dead is structurally obliged to follow it. She has followed it for four centuries, which means her entire practice has a rhythm that is somebody else's livestock, and when the herd is late she is not able to meditate, not able to rest, and not able to be in a settlement, and she has spent four centuries learning to be somewhere that does not need her until it does.
history: Brought up on a graveyard hinterland in a household that enters its dead as one declared group rather than keeping a roll, so her own name was entered in the family's dead while she was still small enough to be carried.

Took work at an execution ground at nineteen, because that is where the throughput is, and learned inside the first year that she cannot tell hunger from a full gut until she is already on the ground and unable to be got up.

Began Still Point at twenty-six, because every manual recommends it and because the Assembly forbids any institution that certifies another body, which left a discipline a person can teach herself as the only kind available to her.

Established at about the eleventh year of that practice that she can perform every step of it and derive nothing from any of them, because qi in this body is never still, including at the moment of release, and continued the practice unchanged.

Published her own throughput figure when the Assembly asked for a figure she did not want published; the figure was the settlement's death rate restated as an appetite, the bench dissolved the same hour without ruling on it, and she has been asked for a second one since.

She can read a stranger's ending back to them in their own words and has never once managed the same for herself. She is the most exact reader on the plains and the only person in the room who knows what her own figure means, and she has begun to find the second fact heavier than the first.

A body whose throughput is entirely a function of the dead is structurally obliged to follow it. A gut-to-marrow conduit with no dantian in it, so qi is never still and the eleventh gate is meaningless rather than closed: it asks about holding and there is no vessel to hold in. The population is held up by the throughput of the dead rather than by births, which makes a conception an event rather than a routine. The soul does not disperse at death, it disperses into whatever killed it, which is the entire basis of the reading trade. A full gut is close to a total loss of function, and this body starves in a clean quiet place, which is the shape of a prosperous city.

Her only discipline is the one thing she cannot do, and her whole practice is a refusal she cannot distinguish from stubbornness.

canon.role_in_story: The shelf is the only ground in the setting where a law is written twice and the second writing is the stronger, and the whole disagreement about that ground is whether a reading of it is stable enough to be evidence. She is the only reader standing on it who can read it at full strength, because a fire body does not need the law to be unambiguous in order to respond to it — it responds to whatever the slot resolves to, including a second resolution. She belongs to a guild whose founding rule is that nothing it makes may be legible to a later composition. So the one reading on the only layer that cannot survive its own composition is being made by the one body that cannot hold a reading at all, and the guild's own art forbids her from explaining either of them to anybody.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the edge of a shelf stone with one hand out flat and close to it, held there for a long time, and answering the question of what she was reading by asking the person who asked it which of the two writings they meant.
canon.lore:
A cinderkin is not descended from anything. It exists where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something in that world metabolises it, which is the reason the setting's elemental law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on cold produces an entirely different animal. Its anatomy is a stable flame with a consistent silhouette — a core, a boundary, and convection lanes that hold a shape — and it has no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense and no fixed mass. Its senses are temperature, fuel and flow, and it has no other channel at all. It does not reproduce; under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks what the world's slot resolves to rather than any birth rate. Qi has no seat in this body, so it is entirely in transit: nothing can be stored in one and nothing can be lost out of one either. The body path is not forbidden, it is simply unavailable, and a cinderkin that attempts it disperses and re-forms smaller. The mind is the only place this body grows, and it is unusually clear, because there is nothing at all between an impulse and the air.

What she stands on explains her species better than her species explains itself. Ten law slots sit over six groups, which leaves four duplicate imprints the surface cannot carry, so the surplus rises, pools and settles on a second layer, and that layer is ground. It is not a mountain: it is a place with its own law list, and the surplus is a property of the list. The drift pools upward, drifts and settles, and behaves like weather rather than like a river, so the shelf is simply where the drift has finished pooling and shelf and drift are one thing at two stages. Because it is a flow, holding it means holding the delivery rather than the destination. And this is the only ground in the setting where a law is written twice and the second writing wins, which is why anything that must not fail is built here and anything that must fail is built one layer down on purpose. The access cost is the whole difficulty: the surface cannot support what is held on the shelf, so anything standing up here is being measured against four imprints the ground below it does not have.

A body trained against a set that is written twice meets a reading that overwrites the one it learned. That is the finding, and she was constituted into it rather than trained into it: she did not arrive on the shelf with a reading that the second writing overwrote, she was constituted on the shelf by a slot that was already being written twice, and everything she has ever read has had a predecessor that it replaced. Her species is the instrument that could settle this and her species is the reason it cannot be settled. An elemental body answers to whatever the slot resolves to and needs no agreement to do it, so she reads the shelf at full strength and reports a value every time, and there is no reservoir anywhere in her in which to hold one report against the next. A cinderkin's reading is an instant with no predecessor. So the whole question of whether the layer's reading is stable enough to be evidence reduces to a comparison she is the only body on the shelf equipped to make and structurally unable to make.

Which is the ground her guild stands on. The guild makes boundary art for the tiers and re-masters its own symbols every generation, so that nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw. Its working medium is marks on unwritable surfaces and its teaching is gestures a listener cannot record. A work is finished when it would mean nothing to anyone who learned it elsewhere. An apprentice is not praised: praise means the work has become readable, and praise is immediately followed by a demand that it be broken. There are no signatures, because identity is the one thing a signature should never be attached to. The studios have no corner and no door. Nothing made is held past its second generation without being broken in public, and the Breaking is a festival whose attendance the guild considers cheerful and therefore a lapse. And no member explains a piece to an outsider, on the stated ground that explanation is the form of the art. She belongs to that, and the thing she has to say is exactly the thing that guild is built not to permit anyone to say.

So she has one discipline and it is the wrong instrument in the best possible way. Revelation Lance is a single named fact driven hard enough to be believed, almost pure light, carried on the intent rather than the will, and it lands on illusions and sceptics alike. She has exactly one named fact. The ground under her writes the same law twice and the second writing wins. She cannot corroborate it, because there is nowhere in her to hold a first reading for comparison, and she cannot explain it, because her guild forbids it. The only route left is to drive it, and driving it is what this technique is for, and there is a price nobody has written down. A belief carried on intent lands on illusions. The guild's entire output is an illusion deliberately made one law short of being legible. She is a fire body, so the light half of the lance is hers by affinity rather than by training, and the half that lands on sceptics is the half that works on her own guild.

And there is a further reason the guild cannot witness her, which is older than her. The highest office in the setting may name a seat and may not take one, and there is no procedure anywhere for a seat offered and refused. A vacancy with no refusal procedure can only be filled by acceptance, which is why the office that names the unfilled seats certifies vacancy and never availability: availability is a thing with a form, and a declined seat is a thing with a witness. One perpetuity survives only because its holder was never actually offered anything, so the setting has never seen a refusal recorded. Her guild produces no witness to anything by design — no signature, no explanation, nothing held past its second generation, nothing that survives to be the second reading. She is therefore the one person on the shelf who is constitutionally incapable of being the witness that question requires, and she is the one person standing there who can supply the answer to it.
history: Came into existence on the second layer where the elemental slot resolves to fire and is already seated twice, with no parent, no cast and no account of how, which is why no record of her begins with a birth.

Was found by the guild in the first generation of its presence on the shelf and taken in, because a body that reads the duplicate imprints at full strength is worth more to a boundary-art house than any teacher it has, and the guild's rule about not explaining a piece saved everyone from the question of what she is.

Noticed in her second decade that every value she read had had a predecessor that it replaced, and began keeping the readings in a sequence rather than a list, on the theory that a sequence might survive her in a way a list would not.

Was asked to state her reading for a certification and could not, because stating it would have required explaining the guild's work and no member of the guild may explain a piece to an outsider, so she gave the number alone and the number was refused as uncorroborated.

Worked out, late and by arithmetic rather than by looking, that the one reading on the only layer where the law is written twice cannot survive its own composition, and that she is the one body present that cannot hold a reading at all, and has kept working without deciding whether that makes her the most reliable witness or the least.
